title: Korea Nuri launch vehicle
summary: Korea's domestically developed orbital rocket, and the path to a reusable successor.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

The Nuri, or KSLV-II, flew successfully in 2022 and 2023, making Korea a country with an independently developed orbital launch capability. It is a three-stage liquid rocket and has carried commercial and government payloads. Korea is now planning a reusable successor and has stood up a national space agency, shifting from a test programme to an industry policy.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2021–2032
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Launch autonomy is a policy good before it is a commercial one; the customer is the state until prices fall.

What Would Change The View

  • Cadence of commercial missions.
  • Reusable successor funding.
  • Private launch entrants in Korea.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
